--- title: "Bar charts" format: html editor: visual --- #### Set up ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(ggpubr) data(mpg) ``` ::: Every row in mpg is a car, every column a feature of that car. mpg stands for miles per gallon. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} head(mpg) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 11 manufacturer model displ year cyl trans drv cty hwy fl class 1 audi a4 1.8 1999 4 auto(l5) f 18 29 p compa… 2 audi a4 1.8 1999 4 manual(m5) f 21 29 p compa… 3 audi a4 2 2008 4 manual(m6) f 20 31 p compa… 4 audi a4 2 2008 4 auto(av) f 21 30 p compa… 5 audi a4 2.8 1999 6 auto(l5) f 16 26 p compa… 6 audi a4 2.8 1999 6 manual(m5) f 18 26 p compa… ``` ::: :::
## Basics of bar charts These uses the geom_col() function to display values *in* the data, geom_bar() to count the cases in a group. In this example, average highway miles per gallon (hwy) is displayed by a the type of car (class). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} (hwy_class <- mpg %>% group_by(class) %>% summarise_at(vars(hwy), list(average_hwy= ~round(mean(.x), digits = 1)))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 7 × 2 class average_hwy 1 2seater 24.8 2 compact 28.3 3 midsize 27.3 4 minivan 22.4 5 pickup 16.9 6 subcompact 28.1 7 suv 18.1 ``` ::: :::
### A basic bar chart That data is then fed to ggplot to produce a simple bar chart. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
### A horizontal bar chart ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy)) + coord_flip() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
## Amend fill colour
#### Standard gglot colours ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, fill=class) + geom_col(width=0.5, colour = "black") + theme_minimal() plot ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### Other options ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggarrange( plot + scale_fill_grey() + theme(legend.position="none"), plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette="PuRd") + theme(legend.position="none"), plot + scale_fill_brewer(palette="Blues") + theme(legend.position="none"), ncol = 1, nrow = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
### Fill by another variable ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} (hwy_class_year <- mpg %>% group_by(class, year) %>% summarise_at(vars(hwy), list(average_hwy_year = ~round(mean(.x), 1)))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 14 × 3 # Groups: class [7] class year average_hwy_year 1 2seater 1999 24.5 2 2seater 2008 25 3 compact 1999 27.9 4 compact 2008 28.7 5 midsize 1999 26.5 6 midsize 2008 28 7 minivan 1999 22.5 8 minivan 2008 22.2 9 pickup 1999 16.8 10 pickup 2008 16.9 11 subcompact 1999 29 12 subcompact 2008 27.1 13 suv 1999 17.6 14 suv 2008 18.6 ``` ::: :::
The second variable is now the fill colour. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class_year, aes(x=class, y=average_hwy_year, fill=year)) + geom_col(width=0.5, colour="black") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
The position argument (setting dodge2) moves the bars to appear alongside each other rather than stacked. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot <- ggplot(data=hwy_class_year, aes(x=class, y=average_hwy_year, fill=year)) + geom_bar(stat="identity", position = "dodge2") plot ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
## Adding labels to data The geom_text function is what adds the labels: - had to move the aes() bit out of the geom_bar() bit to make this work.\ - the vjust bit moves it above and below the bar. A lower minus number would be higher above the bar. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy), vjust=-1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
Here the label is below the bar, vjust=1.5. The colour has been switched to white and the size increased also. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy) + geom_bar(stat="identity") + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy), vjust=1.5, colour="white", size=6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: #### Adding them to our dodged plot above. We also have to 'dodge' the position of the labels within geom_text, again in the position argument. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot + geom_text(aes(label=average_hwy_year), vjust=1.6, color="white", position = position_dodge2(0.9), size=3.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672} ::: :::

## Other formatting
### Bar width Amend bar width within geom_col argument with 'width'. The default is 0.9, smaller values make bars smaller. Max = 1 and removes all space between bars. If you make the entire graph wider or narrower, the bar dimensions will scale proportionally. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} more_space <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), width=0.9) less_space <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), width=0.5) ggarrange(more_space, less_space, ncol = 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
### Change colours In the below the colour affects only the outline, without the fill the bars would be dark grey still. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), colour="blue", fill="white", width = 0.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
Or bar colour can be changed by groups. - Add colour=var, where var is the variable you want to vary the colours by. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, colour=class) + geom_col(fill="white", width=0.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
### Apply themes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy), fill="steelblue") p + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
## Select categories to show You can also select which items to show: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=hwy_class) + geom_col(mapping=aes(x=class, y=average_hwy, label=average_hwy)) + scale_x_discrete(limits=c("suv", "minivan", "pickup")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in geom_col(mapping = aes(x = class, y = average_hwy, label = average_hwy)): Ignoring unknown aesthetics: label ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: Removed 4 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range (`geom_col()`). ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
## Alternative statistics
#### Barplot of counts Similar to a histogram, the stat="bin" command allows ggplot() to work like table(), but specifically for *numeric* values. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=mpg) + aes(x=cyl) + geom_bar(stat="bin") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=672} ::: :::
Or with *character* values, try geom_bar without an argument. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(data=mpg) + aes(x=class) + geom_bar() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=672} ::: :::

## Worked plots ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(haven) library(labelled) library(here) bsa <- readRDS(here::here("data", "synthetic_bsa_2017.rds")) # names(bsa) ``` :::

### Bar chart for 1 way crossbreak (or for a frequency table) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} (leftrigh <- bsa %>% mutate(dolefidl = as_factor(dolefidl), leftrigh = case_when(leftrigh == 9 ~ NA, TRUE ~ zap_labels(leftrigh))) %>% group_by(dolefidl) %>% summarise(leftrigh = mean(leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE), n = n())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 7 × 3 dolefidl leftrigh n 1 Agree strongly 2.25 162 2 Agree 2.48 626 3 Neither agree nor disagree 2.63 1155 4 Disagree 2.60 1007 5 Disagree strongly 2.10 233 6 Not answered 2.17 72 7 NaN 733 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dynamic_str_wrap <- function(text, plot_width = 7, num_labels = 1, char_width = 0.1, margin = 0.1) { max_label_width <- (plot_width * (1 - margin)) / num_labels max_chars <- max_label_width / char_width str_wrap(text, width = floor(max_chars)) } wrap_titles <- function(title, plot_width = 7, char_width = 0.09) { max_chars <- floor(plot_width / char_width) wrapped_title <- str_wrap(title, width = max_chars) return(wrapped_title) } num_labels <- length(levels(fct_drop(leftrigh$dolefidl))) x_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(leftrigh[1])]]) x_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(x_lab) y_lab <- var_label(bsa[[names(leftrigh[2])]]) y_lab_wrap <- wrap_titles(y_lab, plot_width = 5) title <- paste0(y_lab, " by ", x_lab) title_wrap <- wrap_titles(title) buffer <- mean(leftrigh$leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE) / 4 ylim <- c(0, ceiling(max(leftrigh$leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE) + buffer)) (plot <- leftrigh %>% filter(!is.na(dolefidl)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = map_chr(as.character(dolefidl), dynamic_str_wrap, plot_width = 7, num_labels = num_labels, char_width = 0.08, margin = 0.1)) %>% mutate(dolefidl = factor(dolefidl, levels = unique(dolefidl))) %>% ggplot(aes(x = dolefidl, y = leftrigh)) + geom_col() + geom_text(aes(label = round(leftrigh, 1)), vjust = -1.5, size = 11, size.unit = "pt") + theme_gray() + labs(title = title_wrap, x = x_lab_wrap, y = y_lab_wrap) + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) + theme( plot.margin = margin(1,1,1,1), text = element_text(size = 11), # This seems to have no effect??? plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10), size = 11), axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 10), size = 11) )) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Retrospectivly add colour plot + geom_col(fill = "#619CFF") # ggplot blue ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-2.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot + geom_col(fill = "#7082d4") # natcen blue ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-3.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot + geom_col(aes(fill = dolefidl)) + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-4.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot + geom_col(aes(fill = dolefidl)) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-5.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### Bar chart for 2 way crosstab - clustered ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} (leftrigh_sex <- bsa %>% mutate(dolefidl = as_factor(dolefidl), leftrigh = case_when(leftrigh == 9 ~ NA, TRUE ~ zap_labels(leftrigh)), sex = as_factor(Rsex)) %>% group_by(sex, dolefidl) %>% summarise(leftrigh = mean(leftrigh, na.rm = TRUE), n = n())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` `summarise()` has grouped output by 'sex'. extract blue npi <- nc_colours[,2] nmg <- nc_colours[,3] npu <- nc_colours[,4] nor <- nc_colours[,5] nbl_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),1] # extract blue npi_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),2] nmg_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),3] npu_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),4] nor_oppo2 <- nc_colours[c(1,4),5] nbl_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),1] # extract blue npi_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),2] nmg_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),3] npu_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),4] nor_seq3 <- nc_colours[c(1,3,5),5] ncl_5to1 <- unlist(c(as.vector(nc_colours[1,]), as.vector(nc_colours[2,]), as.vector(nc_colours[3,]), as.vector(nc_colours[4,]), as.vector(nc_colours[5,]))) %>% unname ncl_oppo2 <- nc_colours %>% slice(1,4) %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything()) %>% arrange(name) %>% select(-name) %>% as_vector() %>% unname ncl_seq3 <- nc_colours %>% slice(1,3,5) %>% pivot_longer(cols = everything()) %>% arrange(name) %>% select(-name) %>% as_vector() %>% unname # Two functions for diverging colours, Natcen... scale_fill_ga_diverging <- function(low_color = npi[1], medium_color = "white", high_color = nmg[1]) { scale_fill_gradient2(low = low_color, mid = medium_color, high = high_color) } scale_fill_ga_diverging <- function(low_color = nbl[1,5], medium_color = "white", high_color = nor[1,1]) { scale_fill_gradient2(low = low_color, mid = medium_color, high = high_color) } plot + scale_fill_manual(values = ncl_oppo2[7:8]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot + scale_fill_manual(values = nbl) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-2.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot + scale_fill_manual(values = nbl_oppo2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-3.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} plot + scale_fill_manual(values = ncl_5to1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](4_bar_charts_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-4.png){width=672} ::: :::

### Exploration of **str_wrap** Takes a positive integer giving the target line width (in number of characters).
